description.texte: Active representation of Ynov Campus at various promotional and institutional events - student fairs, open house days, and prospective student meet-and-greets. This role involves managing a stand, presenting the school and its programmes to high school students, career changers, and their families, as well as leading guided tours of the campus to showcase classrooms and student life spaces.

Welcoming prospective students and their families is at the heart of this mission, with the goal of creating a trusting atmosphere conducive to open conversations. A detailed presentation of the cybersecurity curriculum is provided, covering the course structure, available specialisations, career prospects, admission requirements, and the opportunities offered by this fast-growing sector.

Personal experience of campus life is shared through first-hand accounts of student daily life, clubs and associations, housing, and extracurricular activities, offering an authentic overview of the programme. Individualised guidance is provided to prospective students by actively listening to their career goals and directing them toward the course or specialisation that best fits their profile.

Academic project simulating a real enterprise environment, carried out in a fully virtualised setup. The objective was to design a web application and deploy an end-to-end operational network infrastructure, covering system administration, network services, and access security.

Deployment of a Windows Server with full Active Directory integration for centralised account and resource management. Group policies (GPO) were defined to control client workstations, while an IPSec VPN was configured to secure remote communications, alongside DNS and DHCP services for name resolution and automatic address assignment.

Implementation of a global security policy covering access rights, network filtering, and firewall rules to ensure the consistency and robustness of the entire system. Configurations were validated in accordance with enterprise infrastructure hardening best practices for a multi-site environment.

Project lead for a team of 8, tasked with designing and deploying a SIEM connected to an online platform allowing each registered user to view the security alerts raised for their session. Coordination between technical and functional teams relied on rigorous deliverable tracking throughout the full development cycle, from scoping to final delivery.

Automated attack scripts were developed to launch simulations against an intentionally vulnerable machine (Metasploitable 3). These scenarios generated real security events, collected, indexed, and visualised via the ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Kibana), feeding the platform with authentic and varied attack data.

Each registered user on the platform received personalised alerts corresponding to the attacks simulated on their session, with detailed information on the nature of the detected threat. The educational goal was to enable analysis of alert feeds, understanding of the underlying attack mechanisms, and discovery of the appropriate defence strategies for each threat type.

INCA is a web platform providing security audit scripts and task automation tools, aimed at both companies and educational institutions looking to train their teams or integrate these tools directly into the management of their information systems. The script library, accessible online, is designed to simplify and standardise recurring technical operations in professional or educational environments.

Contribution to the web platform development using a React and TypeScript stack, taking ownership of front-end features in line with the team's code quality standards. Development was carried out in short iterations, integrated into the collaborative workflow via GitLab, including reviewing merge requests from team members before merging into the main branch.

Development of two original Bash scripts integrated into the platform. The first enables full setup and management of a SQL database from the command line - creating the database, managing tables, adding and manipulating data, all without requiring a graphical interface. The second simplifies firewall rule configuration by providing an interactive command-line interface to define, modify, and apply network filtering rules in a guided and reproducible way.

Oraxya was a free, publicly accessible platform listing real-time prices for Mounjaro and Wegovy across pharmacies in mainland France and overseas territories (DOM/TOM). Closed in June 2026, it served as a unique resource for patients and healthcare professionals looking to locate and compare the availability of these treatments across hundreds of partner pharmacies.

Full-stack contribution to the platform using a Vite and TypeScript stack, covering both front-end development and back-end features. Key deliverables included the design and integration of an interactive map allowing users to geographically visualise medication availability by pharmacy, alongside data ingestion, sorting, and cleaning of datasets submitted by partner pharmacies.

Audits of the existing back-end code were conducted to identify weaknesses, inconsistencies, and optimisation opportunities. Contributions were integrated through a code review process on GitHub, ensuring the maintainability and coherence of the overall codebase.

Second seasonal contract with the City of Marseille's sanitation services, with a marked increase in autonomy compared to the first season. Prior experience allowed for faster integration into the teams and better anticipation of the operational constraints specific to the field.

Maintaining cleanliness of public spaces in high-footfall areas, with direct responsibility for the logistics of collecting and sorting bulky waste for recovery. Rigorous application of HSE standards in a physically intensive environment, with greater initiative taken in organising rounds and handling unexpected situations.

First immersion in the working world as part of the City of Marseille's sanitation services, under a seasonal contract. This experience provided an initial concrete encounter with professional demands - thoroughness, punctuality, following instructions - in a physically challenging work environment.

Active participation in maintaining and cleaning public spaces, handling the collection and sorting of bulky waste for recovery. Application of HSE procedures and integration into a field team working through the intense heat of summer.

Versatile position at Bistrot Les Iris in Bron, with direct responsibility for the quality of the customer experience from welcome to checkout, in a high-footfall establishment. The constant focus on satisfaction and loyalty required ongoing attention to service quality, a strong ability to read customer expectations, and a capacity to handle tense situations with composure and professionalism.

Simultaneous management of floor service and the bar, requiring rigorous organisation to maintain order flow during peak hours. Preparing drinks and light food required mastery of counter techniques and efficient priority management to maintain a fast service without compromising quality.

Strict compliance with HACCP standards in both the kitchen and at the counter, ensuring food safety and hygiene at all times. These regulatory requirements were monitored daily and naturally embedded into working practices.

Photographic coverage of a conference on freelance status in graphic design, held at the Musée d'Art Contemporain (MAC) in Lyon. The goal was to capture the atmosphere of the event and the key moments of the presentations through discreet, precise shooting in a venue with constrained lighting.

Visual documentation of an artistic exhibition evening at the KOMMET space, requiring autonomous management of framing and exposure under variable and low-light conditions. The assignment demanded constant adaptation to the movement of attendees and the evolving ambiance throughout the evening.

Both assignments, carried out over three days, required constant adaptation to each venue's specifics and the ability to produce quality visuals in real time, without any prior staging. All shots were handled entirely independently, from equipment setup to file delivery.

Live photographic coverage of a stage performance by artist Fifamé (slam and spoken word), managing intense and ever-changing stage lighting. Reactivity and anticipation of the artist's movements were essential to capturing the highlights of a constantly evolving performance.

Creation of institutional and artistic portraits to build the artist's digital identity, including official profile photos for distribution platforms and communication materials. Preliminary discussions with the artist helped orient the shoot toward an aesthetic consistent with her creative universe.

Retouching and optimisation of all produced visuals, adapted to both print constraints and web and social media platform specifications. Final delivery respected agreed deadlines and the visual identity established in advance with the artist.

Primary photographer for the BDS (Bureau Des Sports), the school's independent sports association, responsible for covering all events organised by the association - competitions, evenings, and sports meetups. Shoots also included portraits of board members, used to promote the team to students and partners.

Active contribution to the association's Instagram editorial line, selecting visuals, formatting posts, and proposing formats suited to social media usage. This community manager role, complementary to photography, ensured visual consistency between covered events and their online recap.

This six-month mission required a dual photographer and community manager role, with autonomous management of equipment, image sorting, and content publishing. The constant goal was to strengthen the association's visibility and image among students.

Co-president of the BDS (Bureau Des Sports) for a five-month term, in charge of two combined roles within the board - secretary and community manager. The secretary role covered the association's administrative management, partnership follow-up, and drafting contracts with external partners.

Organisation and coordination of the association's sports and social events, from preparation through to execution, working alongside other board members and involved partners. This responsibility required rigorous management of deadlines and available resources.

Management of the association's Instagram communication, publishing content and speaking directly to the student community during events. This dual secretary and community manager role required strong versatility and constant coordination with the rest of the board.

Academic project to design and deploy a secure network architecture within the Ynov Campus Lyon premises, built from scratch through to final acceptance testing. Defining the dedicated IP addressing plan and the network segmentation strategy formed the first phase, establishing the logical foundations of the entire infrastructure.

Configuration of Cisco routers and switches to handle routing and switching within the network, with VLAN segmentation implemented to isolate traffic by user profile (administration, students, guests). Inter-VLAN routing was then configured to allow authorised communication between segments.

Configuration of the Stormshield firewall with precise filtering rules to control and secure all inbound and outbound traffic. The defined access policies ensured global consistency between the network segmentation and security rules, covering all use cases within the campus.

Participation in a 48-hour digital investigation challenge designed as a simulated police inquiry involving cybercrime. The exercise required reconstructing the precise timeline of a fictional case, identifying those involved, and gathering exploitable digital evidence within a framework demanding strict time and priority management.

Analysis of memory dumps extracted from mobile devices and desktop computers using professional forensic suites - Cellebrite Reader for mobile data and Autopsy for PC environments. Extraction of key artefacts (browsing history, metadata, deleted communications) progressively reconstructed the case timeline.

Steganography challenges embedded in the scenario required identifying and extracting information concealed within multimedia files, further complicating the investigation. All analyses were conducted continuously over 48 hours, demanding sustained concentration and perseverance despite time pressure and increasingly complex leads.

Participation in LYON://BREACH, a Capture The Flag (CTF) competition co-organised by Ynov Campus and HackTheBox, bringing together 33 teams on challenges ranging from Very Easy to Insane. The event ran in an intensive format, with technical scenarios spanning a particularly broad range of cybersecurity disciplines.

As part of team 'Pirate La Boite', 9 out of 15 scenarios were solved and 14 out of 20 flags were validated, for a final ranking of 17th out of 33. These results reflect the team's ability to cover multiple challenge categories while maintaining a methodical approach on the most complex tasks.

Challenges spanned a very wide technical spectrum: web and infrastructure exploitation (pwn), binary reverse engineering (reversing), cryptanalysis, smart contract auditing (blockchain), digital forensics, hardware security, mobile app analysis, satellite communications, and industrial control system security (ICS). This competition was an intensive hands-on exercise at the frontier of cybersecurity and critical systems.

Visual production mission for the ON WHEELS brand, spanning several months of collaboration. Contributions included product photography and packshots for professional communication materials, team portraits, and complete photographic coverage of all official brand events.

Filming and editing of short promotional teasers, as well as production of long-format interviews for the brand's digital channels. Each production required full ownership from shoot to post-production, including editing and colour grading.

The entire art direction, from framing to post-production of both photo and video assets, was handled autonomously. Every deliverable was crafted in keeping with the brand's visual identity and the communication team's strategic guidelines, ensuring overall consistency across all materials.

Photographic coverage of the official Ynov Campus Lyon graduation ceremony, carried out as a volunteer assignment. Responsibilities were focused exclusively on raw capture in the field, while sorting and post-production were handled by a dedicated team.

Shooting conditions presented significant technical challenges: high-contrast stage lighting, low ambient light in audience movement zones, and the pace imposed by the ceremony's schedule. Graduate portraits were captured on the fly during each stage appearance, requiring constant adjustment of framing and camera settings to ensure quality in every shot.

competences_obtenir: Technical shooting in low light & high contrast (Events)

description.texte: Designed and implemented, self-taught during high school, a modular multi-agent ecosystem simulation framework using Python and Tkinter, extending Conway's Game of Life principles into a complex survival AI environment.
Engineered a procedural multi-tier terrain grid system managing dynamic plant growth, vegetation mechanics, and physical movement constraints based on terrain speed dampening.

Developed a complete AI state machine for 4 distinct species (herbivores, omnivores, and carnivores) incorporating real-time sensory perception, metabolism, energy tracking, age-based reproduction, and hunting behaviors.

Built a dual-mode execution engine featuring a live real-time Tkinter GUI with execution controls (pause, step, reset), a high-speed headless data collection engine, and a performance benchmarking suite.

Providing on-site and remote IT support for the whole campus, covering level 0 and level 1. Handling incidents and requests through the ticketing system, monitoring and processing the CAMPUS backlog, with occasional reinforcement of the Mérignac HEADQUARTERS or other campuses during overload periods. Interventions are carried out remotely via RustDesk or directly with users, including guiding them through topics such as multi-factor authentication (MFA).

Preparing, imaging and deploying user workstations on Windows (laptops, Surface devices, towers), with tracking of Collaborateurs and PC3D deployments and software installation via FOG. The fleet is tracked daily in GLPI (production, maintenance, stock), including stock verification, equipment organization and inventory, as well as obsolescence management.

Carrying out specific checks on PC3D workstations: Wake On LAN verification, BIOS password checks, PXE boot verification, screw fastening and physical security checks, as well as peripheral verification. Equipment labeling and GLPI inventory updates on status changes, stock, production or maintenance.

Creating user accounts in the identity repository, placing and validating orders with vendors, receiving and shipping equipment, and tracking the PRONOTE status file. Writing and updating procedures, producing technical diagrams, identifying issues and proposing improvements to strengthen support quality and efficiency.
